The resulting papillary muscle displacement leads to tethering of the mitral valve leaflets and mitral regurgitation. Which one of the following statements regarding ischaemic mitral regurgitation is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The presence of ischemic mitral regurgitation following myocardial infarction is associated with a 5-year mortality in excess of 60%.
options.explanation: This reflects the adverse prognosis reported in historical post-infarction ischaemic mitral regurgitation cohorts, which is the intended teaching point.

options.label: B
options.text: 5-year survival is superior for patients who undergo repair of mitral valve in chronic ischemic mitral regurgitation compared to mitral valve replacement.
options.explanation: A survival advantage of repair over chordal-sparing replacement is not established as a general rule; repair also carries a greater risk of recurrent regurgitation in severe secondary disease.

options.label: C
options.text: Chordal cutting increases the incidence of late recurrent mitral regurgitation and negatively impacts postoperative left ventricular function.
options.explanation: Selected secondary-chordal cutting has been studied to relieve leaflet tethering, not as a treatment expected uniformly to worsen recurrence and ventricular function.

options.label: D
options.text: An end-diastolic dimension more than 45 mm is associated with poor reverse remodeling following coronary artery bypass grafting even in the presence of viable myocardium.
options.explanation: A fixed 45 mm end-diastolic dimension is not the established general threshold for poor reverse remodelling; much greater ventricular dilatation is usually implicated.

options.label: E
options.text: Tenting height more than 2.5 mm on echocardiography is a predictor of recurrent regurgitation following repair.
options.explanation: The stated 2.5 mm height is not the usual threshold. A tenting area around 2.5 square centimetres and a coaptation or tenting height around 10 mm are the commonly discussed adverse measurements.

questions.explanation: Ischaemic mitral regurgitation after myocardial infarction is a marker of adverse ventricular remodelling and poor prognosis; historical cohorts reported five-year mortality above 60%. That population estimate is not an individual prediction and varies with severity and contemporary treatment.

Which one of the following statements regarding ART is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: There was a statistically significant decrease in 30-day mortality after off-pump CABG compared to on-pump CABG.
options.explanation: No significant reduction in early mortality with off-pump surgery was demonstrated in this comparison.

options.label: B
options.text: There was a significant increase in stroke rates after 1 year in the on- pump CABG group compared to off-pump CABG group.
options.explanation: A significant increase in one-year stroke after on-pump surgery was not demonstrated.

options.label: C
options.text: There was a statistically significant increase in the need for intra-aortic balloon pump and renal support after on-pump CABG.
options.explanation: The need for intra-aortic balloon support and renal support did not differ significantly between the techniques.

options.label: D
options.text: A similar average number of grafts were performed with on- and off- pump surgery.
options.explanation: A similar graft count was achieved with both techniques, which is the finding selected by the source.

options.label: E
options.text: Repeat revascularisation was significantly higher in off-pump patients at 30 days and at 1 year.
options.explanation: Repeat revascularization was numerically higher after off-pump surgery, but the reported differences did not establish the asserted significant increase at both time points.

questions.explanation: In the ART secondary comparison of operative techniques, on-pump and off-pump patients received a similar number of grafts, with a median of three. ART randomized mammary-artery strategy, not the choice of on-pump versus off-pump surgery.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with normal preoperative left ventricular function has just returned to the intensive care unit following coronary artery bypass grafting. His intraoperative course was unremarkable. His initial haemodynamic and laboratory data includes: Pulse: 75 beats per minute Pulmonary artery pressure: 35/17 mmHg Haemoglobin: 11 gm/dL Pulmonary artery wedge pressure: 13 mmHg Blood pressure: 130/84 mmHg Cardiac index: 1.7 L/[min*m2] Systemic vascular resistance index: 4100 dynes sec cm-5/m2 The most appropriate initial treatment of this patient is

options.label: A
options.text: 250 cc fluid bolus for volume expansion.
options.explanation: A routine fluid bolus is less compelling when the wedge pressure is already adequate and excessive afterload is the obvious abnormality. Filling and ventricular function still need bedside reassessment.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dobutamine can raise cardiac output but may not be the best first response to marked vasoconstriction in a patient with preserved baseline ventricular function and adequate pressure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Epinephrine increases myocardial oxygen demand and may aggravate vasoconstriction; it is not the obvious first choice for this high-resistance, normotensive profile.

options.label: D
options.explanation: At sufficient doses nitroglycerin can reduce vascular resistance and improve coronary supply, but its predominant venodilator effect may reduce preload. This remains the original key, not a uniquely proven choice.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Sodium nitroprusside is a potent, titratable arterial and venous dilator and is a plausible preferred treatment for excessive afterload. It cannot fairly be dismissed as wrong from the supplied data.

questions.explanation: The dominant haemodynamic abnormality is a very high systemic vascular resistance with low cardiac index and adequate filling pressure. Titrated vasodilation can improve forward flow, but the original nitroglycerin key is not uniquely compelled; sodium nitroprusside more directly reduces arterial afterload.

questions.reviewNote: Original D key is not clearly superior to E for low output with markedly elevated afterload. Preserve it, but hold grading pending source/clinical review rather than inventing a reason that nitroprusside is wrong.

His initial arterial blood gas reveals: pH of 7.49; pO2 160 mmHg; pCO2 35 mmHg The most important initial ventilatory adjustment is to decrease the

options.label: A
options.explanation: Oxygen can subsequently be titrated down with a PaO2 of 160 mm Hg, but this does not address the excessive tidal volume and mechanical-stress concern.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Shortening inspiratory time does not directly correct the very large delivered tidal volume and can increase peak flow and peak airway pressure.

options.label: C
options.text: positive end-expiratory pressure to 5 cm H2O.
options.explanation: Reducing PEEP is not the principal response to an excessively large tidal volume and may worsen recruitment.

options.label: D
options.text: respiratory rate to 10 beats per minute.
options.explanation: A lower rate reduces minute ventilation but leaves the potentially injurious volume of each breath unchanged.

options.label: E
options.explanation: This directly reduces overdistension and minute ventilation. A final protective volume should be individualized to predicted body weight, often lower than 700 mL.

questions.explanation: The immediate concern is the excessive 1,000 mL tidal volume and high inspiratory pressure. questions.stem: A 69-year-old man is scheduled to undergo elective myocardial revascularisation. On preoperative physical examination he has a high- pitched, moderately loud right carotid bruit. He denies any neurological symptoms. Duplex ultrasound shows a 50% stenosis of the right internal carotid artery just above the bifurcation of the common carotid artery. Which of the following is the most appropriate plan for the management of this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: cancel myocardial revascularisation and obtain a carotid angiogram
options.explanation: This degree of asymptomatic stenosis does not in itself justify cancelling CABG or obtaining invasive carotid angiography.

options.label: B
options.text: proceed with carotid artery repair and reschedule myocardial revascularisation
options.explanation: Carotid repair is not indicated simply because a moderate, asymptomatic stenosis accompanies coronary disease.

options.label: C
options.text: proceed with myocardial revascularisation and follow up with serial Duplex examinations
options.explanation: Proceeding with CABG and following the carotid disease, alongside medical risk reduction, is the appropriate listed strategy.

options.label: D
options.text: proceed with simultaneous myocardial revascularisation and carotid artery repair
options.explanation: Simultaneous carotid repair adds procedural risk without a demonstrated indication for this asymptomatic 50% lesion.

options.label: E
options.text: stage myocardial revascularisation and carotid artery repair
options.explanation: Staging a carotid operation still exposes the patient to an unnecessary intervention for the described lesion.

questions.explanation: An asymptomatic 50% internal carotid stenosis is generally managed medically with surveillance, not prophylactic carotid intervention solely to permit CABG. The patient can proceed with the indicated coronary revascularization after appropriate multidisciplinary assessment.

questions.stem: A 64 years old patient with a 2 cm lung cancer, negative lymph nodes on CT staging and diminished pulmonary reserve needs a pulmonary resection. In view of the diminished pulmonary reserve, the decision was taken to perform segmentectomy. Which one of the following statements regarding segmentectomy is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: equivalent local recurrence rate when compared to lobectomy
options.explanation: Local recurrence has often been higher after segmentectomy, including in some modern comparisons, despite favourable survival in selected small tumours. Equivalence is not a universal claim.

options.label: B
options.text: fewer pleural space complications when performed without a stapler compared to lobectomy
options.explanation: A nonstapled intersegmental plane can increase air-leak and pleural-space problems; fewer complications cannot be assumed.

options.label: C
options.text: reduced air leakage when performed with the classic stripping technique compared to lobectomy
options.explanation: The classic stripping technique exposes parenchyma and does not reliably reduce air leak relative to lobectomy.

options.label: D
options.text: reduced mortality compared to lobectomy patients
options.explanation: A consistent mortality reduction from segmentectomy itself cannot be assumed; patient selection and limited reserve strongly affect comparative outcomes.

options.label: E
options.text: similar pulmonary function one year after operation compared to lobectomy
options.explanation: Older studies found little durable functional difference, which explains the source key. More recent selected trials have found modest function preservation, so this is not a universal contemporary result.

questions.explanation: The original E key reflects older comparisons in which sublobar resection did not deliver a clear durable pulmonary-function advantage. Contemporary trials of carefully selected small peripheral node-negative cancers show different oncological and functional trade-offs, so the broad statements need an era and patient-selection context.

options.label: A
options.text: Early occlusion rates are similar among patients treated with single therapy or dual anti-platelet therapy.
options.explanation: The historical pooled analysis found fewer early saphenous-vein occlusions with dual therapy, not identical early graft-occlusion rates.

options.label: B
options.text: Single anti-platelet therapy is associated with a significantly increased arterial graft loss compared to dual anti-platelet therapy.
options.explanation: The clearest patency signal was for saphenous-vein grafts; a significant arterial-graft loss difference was not established as stated.

options.label: C
options.text: In-hospital or 30-day mortality is lower with dual anti-platelet therapy compared to single anti-platelet therapy alone.
options.explanation: Lower early mortality was reported in the historical pooled analysis, which explains C, but this association is not a universal causal guarantee.

options.text: Dual anti-platelet therapy is associated with a significantly increased incidence of major bleeding episodes compared to single anti-platelet therapy alone.
options.explanation: Dual therapy can increase major bleeding; the historical analysis showed a borderline signal and later analyses differ. It would be misleading to narrate increased bleeding as categorically false.

questions.explanation: The source key reflects a 2013 pooled analysis reporting lower in-hospital or 30-day mortality with aspirin plus clopidogrel than aspirin alone. questions.stem: The radial artery (RA), as an alternative to the saphenous vein or the right internal thoracic artery (RITA) for coronary artery bypass grafting, has gained considerable interest over the years. Radial Artery Patency Study (RAPS) Investigators sought to determine the relative patency rate of radial-artery and saphenous vein grafts in a randomized trial in which they controlled for bias in the selection of patients and vessels. Which one of the following statements regarding RAPS is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The primary endpoint was all-cause death.
options.explanation: The principal endpoint was angiographic graft occlusion, not all-cause mortality.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Angiography was planned by protocol rather than restricted to patients who developed symptoms.

options.label: C
options.text: Diffuse narrowing of the graft (the angiographic "string sign") was present in 30 percent of radial artery grafts.
options.explanation: The early radial-artery string-sign rate was approximately 7%, not 30%.

options.label: D
options.text: At one year similar graft occlusion rates were observed for radial artery and saphenous vein grafts.
options.explanation: Complete occlusion at one year was less frequent in radial grafts. Functional occlusion was more similar, so the unqualified assertion that occlusion rates were alike misses the trial distinction.

options.label: E

options.explanation: Late functional occlusion was lower with radial arteries than with vein grafts, which is the intended longer-term result.

questions.explanation: RAPS compared paired radial-artery and saphenous-vein grafts with protocol angiography. At late follow-up beyond five years, functional graft occlusion was less frequent with radial grafts.

questions.stem: The retrotracheal space (also known as the Raider triangle or retrotracheal triangle) is a radiolucent area that extends from the thoracic inlet to the aortic arch and is visible on lateral chest radiographs. A wide spectrum of diseases can occur in this region; they may arise either from the normal contents of the retrotracheal space or from adjacent structures. Which one of the following statements regarding the retrotracheal space is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Lungs are a normal content of the retrotracheal space.
options.explanation: Lung is a normal component of the retrotracheal region and helps create its lucent appearance on a lateral radiograph.

options.label: B
options.text: The posterior tracheal line forms the posterior margin of the retrotracheal space.
options.explanation: The posterior tracheal line borders the anterior side of the retrotracheal space.

options.label: C
options.text: The postertior tracheal line is produced by oesophagus in contact with the posterior wall of the trachea.
options.explanation: The posterior tracheal stripe is ordinarily seen when the posterior tracheal wall and adjacent soft tissue are outlined by air. Oesophageal contact can produce a thicker tracheo-oesophageal stripe, a distinct description.

options.label: D
options.text: The most common lesions in the retrotracheal space are neurogenic in origin.
options.explanation: Neurogenic tumours classically arise in the paravertebral posterior mediastinum; they are not the most common general retrotracheal lesion category.

options.label: E
options.text: Right recurrent laryngeal nerve is the most consistent content of the retrotracheal space.
options.explanation: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve is not the most consistent defining content of this radiographic space; its normal course loops around the subclavian artery in the upper mediastinal/root-of-neck region.

questions.explanation: Aerated lung can extend into the retrotracheal region and contributes to its normal radiolucency. The posterior tracheal line is the anterior boundary of this space, not its posterior boundary.
